# Fate UI v0.8.1-beta1

This beta adds a built-in Chromium workspace, brings the main project resources into one navigator, and introduces reusable automations that always open for review before they run.

## Built-in browser workspace

- Opens a real, sandboxed Chromium view beside the conversation, with tabs, history, reload and stop controls, an address bar, local HTML previews, and a resizable split.
- Adds Agent and Annotate modes. Agent mode can navigate, inspect, click, type, press keys, scroll, and list tabs through Pi tools. Annotate mode lets you select rendered elements or regions and attach them to the composer with an editable note.
- Builds bounded semantic snapshots from DOM and accessibility data, gives elements short-lived refs, and revalidates the live document, frame, target, hit point, and permission immediately before input is dispatched.
- Shows a visible virtual pointer for agent clicks. Human mouse or keyboard input pauses agent control, and Escape stops annotation or agent interaction before it affects the active Pi run.
- Keeps browser ownership tied to the selected root session. Switching projects or sessions releases the old lease, cancels pending work, and clears task-scoped access.
- Preserves browser annotation attachments across queued-message edits. Sent annotations are resolved again, redacted, added to the prompt as untrusted page context, and removed from the page only after Pi accepts the message.

## Browser security boundaries

- Uses an isolated, project-derived Chromium profile with Node integration disabled, context isolation and sandboxing enabled, permissions denied, popups intercepted, and developer tools disabled in the managed view.
- Routes HTTP, HTTPS, and WebSocket traffic through a loopback safety proxy that performs its own DNS resolution, pins approved addresses, blocks cloud metadata, and rejects DNS rebinding to private or local networks.
- Requires explicit read or interact grants for Pi. Private-network origins require a separate grant unless the selected session has Full access, and cloud metadata remains blocked in every mode.
- Confirms cross-origin transfers and consequential submit, download, account, communication, destructive, and financial actions. Passwords, one-time codes, payment fields, tokens, and other secret-like input remain blocked outside Full access.
- Serves local HTML, XHTML, and SVG through per-tab capability URLs. Local previews are confined to the selected file directory, use a restrictive content security policy, cannot submit forms or open external pages, and cannot read outside that preview directory.
- Hides and pauses the native page behind application dialogs so Chromium cannot float above a confirmation, settings window, image viewer, or GoalMax editor.

## Sessions, resources, and command center

- Reworks the left pane into persistent Sessions, Automations, and Resources tabs.
- Moves project and session creation into the Sessions toolbar while preserving search, sorting, row actions, conversation paths, and keyboard behavior.
- Adds a Resources navigator for project files, browser tabs, Pi skills, prompts and extension commands, the manual terminal, saved automations, and sessions.
- Expands Ctrl/Cmd+K into a command center that searches commands and resources together. File results open the real project preview, browser results activate the exact tab, and Pi Library items are inserted at the current composer caret without sending the draft.
- Adds honest unavailable and failure feedback for native menu commands, terminal access, browser access, model changes, session creation, and project selection.
- Turns the first-launch Inspect codebase and Ship a change cards into editable starter prompts instead of sending work automatically.

## Reusable project automations

- Adds project-scoped saved automations with create, edit, search, delete, and manual open flows.
- Persists automation data atomically under the Fate UI data directory, validates every stored document, serializes writes per project, bounds prompt and catalog sizes, and isolates projects with canonical path identities.
- Limits automation authority to Read only or Edit project. Full access is never inherited by an automation session.
- Creates and names the new Pi session, applies its final tool and permission boundary, persists that boundary, and only then publishes the session to the UI.
- Restores the saved prompt into the composer for review and never sends it automatically. Launch counts and accepted or failed outcomes stay with the saved definition.
- Keeps large automation catalogs responsive by avoiding full-prompt lowercase copies during search and by rendering bounded prompt previews while still searching the complete saved text.

## GoalMax completion and recovery

- Adds `goalmax_complete` as the explicit final handoff. It accepts current evidence, stops ordinary continuation scheduling, and waits for the root turn to settle before independent verification.
- Keeps the existing completion-candidate report path for compatibility while directing new goals through the dedicated completion gate.
- Records separate verification-passed and goal-completed timeline events.
- Fails closed if root settlement or recovery persistence fails. The goal becomes visibly blocked and non-runnable in memory until the user resumes or rebinds it, rather than continuing with stale state.
- Prevents GoalMax control calls from counting as implementation work or verification evidence.

## Reliability, performance, and packaging

- Prevents temporary Pi queue counts from making queued rows disappear while a message is edited, cancelled, or changed between Follow up and Steer.
- Redacts browser typing and sensitive navigation details from visible tool history.
- Stops native browser-bound polling while the active tab is blank and only observes application dialog mutations while the Browser workspace is open.
- Flushes the current DOM layout before reading Chromium's accessibility tree and viewport so the first semantic snapshot does not mix old and new page state.
- Adds a real PTY exchange to packaged smoke tests so the manual terminal must start, return output, and exit on every supported runner.
- Packages and validates the executable macOS node-pty helper from the same native directory the runtime will load.
- Keeps smoke output bounded without losing required speech, yt-dlp, theme, terminal, or application markers.
- Removes only the exact Fate UI directory from Windows PATH during updates and uninstall. A new installer regression check verifies that similarly named PATH entries remain untouched.
- Updates Mermaid to 11.16.1 and pins the patched js-yaml 4.3.1 build dependency. Production and full dependency audits report no known vulnerabilities.

## Compatibility and installers

Existing projects, Pi sessions, settings, themes, Agent Team data, and Git workflows do not require a manual migration. This beta does not add scheduled or background automations, arbitrary desktop control, or an intentional breaking change.

GitHub Actions builds and tests the release natively on Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon, macOS Intel, and Linux x64. The prerelease contains seven installers plus `SHA256SUMS`:

- Windows x64: NSIS `.exe`
- macOS arm64 and x64: `.dmg` and `.pkg`
- Linux x64: `.AppImage` and `.deb`

Public beta installers remain unsigned. Windows SmartScreen or macOS Gatekeeper may show an unknown-publisher warning, so verify downloads against `SHA256SUMS`.
